cohort: The study included all eclampsia patients admitted to the antenatal ward in JIPMER from October 2009 to May 2011.
finding: The primary finding was a high perinatal mortality rate of 231 per 1000 births among eclamptic women, with prematurity being the most common cause for NICU admissions and neonatal deaths.
mod_finding: 65% of eclamptic women required labor induction, and 20% underwent cesarean section, primarily due to fetal distress.
birth_weight: Average birth weight was 1.825kg, with 100 babies weighing less than 1.5kg and 212 babies less than 2.5kg.
